sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cicollus was a god of the Continental Celts. He was an obscure deity. His name appears to mean a great protector. People worshipped him across central Europe. Roman inscriptions present him as the warrior deity Mars in another form. He may match the guardian god Apollo Anextiomarus. The goddess Litavis was his consort.

okr.objective: Cicollus was a central European god of the Continental Celts linked to Mars and Apollo Anextiomarus.
key_results: His name appears to mean a great protector.
Roman-era inscriptions call him a form of the warrior god Mars.
He may be the same being as the protector god Apollo Anextiomarus.
His consort was the goddess Litavis.
